I'm trying to get a job at Hostgator as a phone support tech and on paper i'm qualified, but i don't have any relevant job experience to show for it. Would a Comptia A+ certification help my chances or is it overhyped?
Is an A+ certification really a desirable trait on a resume?

The headline is different from the story. It depends on what you want to do. Phone support at Hostgator? Sure. Put it on. It's better than nothing. Put down that you worked light for the university drama society. You won't rely on this experience, but it shows some knowledge.

You'll get people talking trash about certs, but.. they're something. You're asking for an entry level job. They'll train you. The cert lets them know you're trainable and you can even self-train.

In my opinion, certifications are like anything else on a resume: They might only serve to "get your foot in the door" and get you to the real deal...the interview.

Personally, and again this is only my opinion, seeing a bunch of certifications on a resume actually counts AGAINST my opinion of a potential candidate. It tends to show that they place more emphasis on reading books and passing tests than using their heads to solve real world problems. I've hired too many of these "certies" only to find that they can't apply any of their supposed tech knowledge in the field. Or, worse yet, they can't deal with the PEOPLE who are having problems with their tech.

Given that all other things between 2 applicants are equal, one person having the A+ cert might be preferred over the person who doesn't have it. That said, all things being equal rarely happens. And actual experience matters much more than a cert.
